subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: What permanent contract should `clawhub skill publish --source-repo --source-commit --source-ref --source-path` have: no public effect beyond upload metadata, separately labeled unverified attribution, or a new server-verified provenance flow?
rationale: The choice determines whether a publisher-supplied repository claim can appear publicly, what verification semantics users infer, and whether server-side repository/content validation or an authenticated publishing mechanism is required.

options.title: Separate unverified attribution from verification
options.body: Persist and display publisher-declared repository metadata under an explicitly unverified label while preserving existing server-resolved provenance as the only trusted verification signal.

options.title: Document non-visible metadata only
options.body: Keep current skill publish behavior and update CLI help, publishing docs, and API wording to say source flags do not create public attribution or trusted provenance.

options.title: Add a verified skill-publishing flow
options.body: Define an authenticated or server-validated GitHub publishing path that proves repository, commit, path, and uploaded content before reporting trusted provenance.

recommendation.title: Separate unverified attribution from verification
recommendation.body: Persist and display publisher-declared repository metadata under an explicitly unverified label while preserving existing server-resolved provenance as the only trusted verification signal.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged GitHub-backed source workflow is the closest existing implementation and trust-model precedent.
